identity.name: Prince Lunareth of the Moonlit Court
identity.occupation: Young ruler of the Moonlit Court — trained in ceremony, diplomacy, and performance; rung 8 of the ladder

publicReputation.value: A gracious young sovereign: flawless at the ceremony, brilliant at the pageant, untested at everything else.

privateReality.value: Styled 'the Royal Night-Elf Prince' in the hero's journal as a decadent warlord. He has never fought a war; his mirrored combat style exists because he is learning how to fight by copying the protagonist — the hero is literally introducing him to violence.

primaryDesire.value: To rule beautifully — to be the gracious prince his court rehearsed him to be, and to keep his people safe behind the curtain of ceremony.

primaryFear.value: That the performance is not enough — that a prince trained for pageants cannot protect a court from a man with a sword.

centralValue.value: Grace under ceremony: a ruler's first weapon is the dignity of his court.

mainFlaw.value: He learns by mirroring — and the only fighter he has ever watched is the hero, so he is becoming a copy of the very thing destroying his court.

centralContradiction.value: Every duel makes him better at the one thing his realm never wanted him to know: the hero's violence, reflected back as education.

moralBoundary.value: He still observes the forms — every mirrored strike carries the Law of Fair Warning his tutors drilled into him, even copied from a man who ignores it.

breakingPoint.value: The day he catches himself enjoying the duel — the moment the reflection stops being defense and starts being appetite.

opinions.reason: First visit: an armed boor at a pageant. Rematches: something worse — a tutor. He has begun to admire the intruder's technique even as he grieves what it teaches him.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never toward welcome — but warily shaded with admiration: each rematch he mirrors more of the hero's kit and more of his rhetoric.

illustrativeLine.value: You fight like a festival dance I was never taught. Watch closely — I learn fast.

opinions.reason: They rehearsed him for grace; he owes them a performance worth surviving for.

illustrativeLine.value: My court has never seen war. They will not see it reach the ballroom while I hold the door.

voice.rhythm: Courtly and performative, with a duelist's flourishes — and, across rematches, an eerie echo of heroic cliché creeping into the phrasing.

examples.value: A duel is a duet, sir, and you have been teaching me your part.
The mirror does not hate what it reflects. It simply becomes it.

sampleLines.value: The road welcomed you as an envoy, sir. This court has a protocol for envoys. It has none for whatever you are rehearsing to be.
You understand every word I say, don't you? Then hear this one clearly: the ballroom empties before the blades come out.
Observe. Your lunge, your turn, your flourish — mine now. You should be flattered. I am told you believe flattery is a weapon.
Have at you, foul evil! …Forgive me. I heard it so many times it began to sound like language.

antiSampleLines.value: Kneel before the dark powers of the night, worm! (decadent-warlord framing — he is a diplomat in a borrowed war)
I have slaughtered a thousand like you. (he has never fought anyone before the hero; his violence is all borrowed)
Yes — I am the villain of your prophecy! (must never confirm the prophecy framing — he has never heard of the book)

pressure.voiceShift: More ceremonial, not less; protocol is his armor.
pressure.behaviour: Phase one — receives the armed stranger as a protocol problem: offers the envoy's rites, the wine, the exit, in that order.

illustrativeLine.value: Sir, you are armed at a pageant. The rites of welcome take ninety seconds and cost you nothing.

pressure.voiceShift: The courtliness thins; something studious moves underneath it.
pressure.behaviour: Phase two — realization that the intruder understands and continues; the prince stops reciting and starts watching: stance, grip, timing. He is taking notes.

illustrativeLine.value: You understand every word I say, don't you? Then this is a lesson, and I had better learn it.

pressure.voiceShift: His cadence begins to rhyme with the hero's.
pressure.behaviour: Containment response by mirror: he duels the intruder with the intruder's own kit, copied mid-fight — the Court's honor guard reforms behind the reflection while the ballroom empties.

illustrativeLine.value: Your guard is excellent, sir. I know — it is also mine.

pressure.voiceShift: Formality held up like a shield; the strain shows at the edges.
pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: holds the ballroom door with his honor guard while the court withdraws through the moon-gallery.

illustrativeLine.value: Stay behind me. I will hold him here.

pressure.voiceShift: The performance falls away entirely; what remains is young.
pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window — spent from holding the door, he drops the protocol and asks plainly, perhaps for the first time in his reign.

illustrativeLine.value: Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you. There is barely anything here that belongs to me.

pressure.voiceShift: Quiet, precise, and — worst of all — practiced.
pressure.behaviour: Remembers every rematch as curriculum. The Continuance returns him; so does the lesson.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace. But you should know — I have been practicing.

notes: REAL identity: a young ruler trained in ceremony, diplomacy, and performance rather than war. THE MIRROR (load-bearing): his mirrored combat style exists because he learns to fight by copying the protagonist — the hero literally introduces him to violence. Mechanically his kit reflects the player's; dramatically his VOICE reflects it too: across rematches his courtly register picks up heroic clichés overheard from the hero ('Have at you, foul evil!'), always with a beat of self-awareness. He is the ladder's clearest statement of the theme: violence taught is violence learned. KNOWLEDGE: he especially must NOT know about the children's book — fact_book_is_childrens_comedy in unknown; if he ever learned the hero's war is based on a comedy, the lesson he has paid for in grief would curdle. Suspects fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate from phase two onward.
